newsitem.title: GERMANY: Condor profits fall 25pct on fuel costs.
newsitem.headline: Condor profits fall 25pct on fuel costs.

text.p: Condor Flugdienst GmbH, the holiday airline unit of Deutsche Lufthansa AG, said pre-tax profits fell 25 percent to 108 million marks ($63 million) in 1996.
Managing director Franz Schoiber said the fall in profits was mostly due to a 25 percent rise in fuel costs of 45 million dollars and high operating fees payable in U.S. dollar-linked currencies.
Stagnating prices and special offers generated by market over-capacity also affected results, he told a news conference.
In 1996, Condor improved passenger numbers 7.1 percent to 6.46 million, increased turnover 3.2 percent to 2.1 billion marks and maintained a 25 percent share of the German package holiday market.
The overall market grew just four percent to 26 million passengers last year due to weak consumer demand, strong price competition and increasing last-minute holiday bookings, Schoiber said.
Condor expected moderate rises in passenger numbers and turnover this year, despite a 10 percent growth over the first four months because of mixed expectations for the summer.
"Short-term bookings are likely, there will be over-capacity on the market and we will react appropriately," Schoiber said.
Demand for Turkey, Egypt and the Balearic Islands was good but bookings for the Canary Islands were below expectations, he added.
